title: Where reflection's cost can and cannot be removed

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: On JDK 18 or later, when can the JIT inline through a call to method.invoke(target)?

options.text: When setAccessible(true) was called on that Method beforehand.
options.says: setAccessible removes the access check, but a Method that is not a constant still goes through an indirect call.

options.text: Never, because Method.invoke stays a native call into the JVM.
options.says: Since JEP 416 Method.invoke is implemented with method handles, which the JIT can inline through.

options.text: When that Method object is held in a static final field.
options.says: A Method in a static final field is a constant to the JIT, which can then inline through the method-handle-based invoke.

questions.stem: A framework caches Method objects in a WeakHashMap<Class<?>, Method> so that plugin classes can unload. What happens when a plugin's class loader is dropped?

options.text: The entries are removed at the next collection, and the plugin classes unload.
options.says: A weak key is only cleared when nothing else holds it, and here the map's own value holds it.

options.text: The entries stay, since each Method keeps its declaring class reachable.
options.says: A Method strongly references its declaring Class, so the value keeps its own key alive and the classes never unload; ClassValue avoids this.

options.text: The Method values are cleared, and the Class keys stay in the map.
options.says: A WeakHashMap holds its values strongly; only keys are weak, so nothing clears the Methods.

concepts: Since JDK 18 Method.invoke is built on method handles, and the JIT inlines through it only when the Method is a constant such as a static final field.
A WeakHashMap keyed by Class does not let classes unload when its values are Methods, because each Method references its declaring class; ClassValue does.
